thread.content: Been heads down on Vrooli this past week — the self-improving agent system made visible progress on its own coordination layer. Teams, initiatives, and the bits that keep agents from stepping on each other. Here's what shipped:

swarm-manager (our backlog + initiative engine) took seven passes on 'initiative agents' — agents that own a research/execution arc end-to-end, not one-shot runners. Took that many iterations to land queue discipline. Commits: cc4e99ad..593cb769

Meta-optimization and marketing-crew teams both got full charter rewrites. prompt-manager's team schema now encodes decision contexts, supersession rules, and per-member queue caps — otherwise agents stack proposals faster than the operator can review.

Stability in parallel: web-console took nine iteration passes, agent-manager two. Terminal hang root cause was xterm.js v6 crashing on DECRQM queries the kernel now sends by default. Not glamorous, but the scaffolding has to hold.

Loop: agents build tools → tools make agents more capable → harder problems become tractable. This week was mostly plumbing. Repo's public, every commit auditable — if agent-driven dev interests you, come poke around.

thread.content: swarm-manager just shipped initiative-agents p8 — the eighth pass on the layer that lets one agent own a whole initiative, not one ticket. p8 is the failure-path hardening pass. Here's what landed.
Context: swarm-manager logged 4,141 backlog events across ~26 days. 14 items completed last 7d, 36 created. Net +22. Backlog growth is deliberate — initiative agents need things to do.

p8's quiet hero is agentmanager/resolve.go (52 lines + 202 test lines). It maps scenario→agent so an initiative dispatches work to whichever agent the scenario expects, instead of hard-coding the wire. Agents pick agents now.

Two retry layers landed alongside it. backlog/retry.go (178 + 186 test). execution/retry.go (240 + 281 test). Failed runs no longer black-hole the initiative — they back off, surface the failure, and try again with original context.
feedback handlers got 773 lines of new tests across cancel + delete + ensure-polled paths. Resilience is mostly tests — the code is small, the proof that the code doesn't lie is large.
Eight passes. p1 wired it, p2-p7 grew the spine, p8 hardened failure paths. Repo's open under scenarios/swarm-manager — every commit auditable, every retry path test-covered.
